notes.decision: The chapter number ⲓⲏ (=18) appears at start (in brackets) and again at line-end (visible). The trailing ⲓⲏ is unexplained — possibly a running-title remnant or scribal repetition. Preserved as written.
ⲉⲓⲣⲉ + 3pl pronominal object 'made/waged them' — referring to the wars. The Sons of Light are subject; the wars are object.
Lycopolitan orthographic variant (ⲫ for ⲑ) of ⲑⲃ̄ⲓⲟ 'humbled' — verb of subjugation, per accumulated glossary. Subject: Sons of Light; object: Sons of Darkness.
Reduplicated ⲁϩⲉ-ⲁϩⲉ 'fight, contend, do battle.' The First Living Man as combatant against the King of Darkness — the standard cosmogonic combat at the origin of the Manichaean drama.
Per glossary entry ⲃⲱⲣⲃ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'be bound upon, fettered upon.' The First Man bound the dark powers upon his tree (the Living Soul) — the cosmological capture of the archons within the captured light.
Read as ⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'soul' — likely a scribal/orthographic confusion of ψ/τ. Combined with ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'living,' yields the standard Manichaean term Living Soul (the captured light bound in matter).
Probably Lyc. ⲧ-ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ or ⲧ-ϩⲱⲣⲃⲥ̄ 'the covering, veil, shadow.' Translated 'the covering' tentatively. Could refer to the cosmic veil/curtain of matter or a covering of the Living Soul.

ⲧⲉϩ- = Lyc. fem. possessive 'his (fem. obj.)'; ⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ = Greek παρθένος 'virgin'. The 'Virgin of Light' / Maiden of Light is here identified with (or paralleled to) the Living Fire — correspondential identification in standard Manichaean fashion.

ⲣ̄-ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'to peep/peer out' (lit. 'do an eye out'). Plural participle: 'those who peer forth.' Refers to the light-particles or souls peering out from the tree (Living Soul) — they then hide like fish (line 14).
ⲧⲃⲧ = ⲧⲏⲃⲧ 'fish' (Lyc. plural ⲍⲛ̄ⲧⲃⲧ 'fish'). Simile for the hidden light-particles concealing themselves like fish in water — standard Manichaean image of the Living Soul scattered through matter.
'The five counsels (ⲥⲁⲝⲛⲉ = ϣⲟϫⲛⲉ) of the five elements (στοιχεῖα).' Per glossary, ⲥⲁⲝⲛⲉ = 'counsel.' The five counsels are likely the Five Sons of First Man corresponding to the five elements.

Greek loanword κολοβός / κάλαβις 'axe, mattock.' Direct quotation in line 18 of Mt 3:10 / Lk 3:9 'the axe is laid at the root of the trees.' The First Man is figured as the apocalyptic axe at the root of the bitter tree (= matter).
Read as ⲥⲱⲧⲏⲣ 'Savior' (Greek σωτήρ). Manichaean appellation for Jesus, who quotes the Baptist's prophetic saying.

'It bears bitter fruits until this very moment.' ⲛⲉϩⲧ likely = ⲛⲁ-ϯ 'will give/bear' or qualitative-bearing form; ⲭⲛ = ϫⲓⲛ 'since/from'; ⲡⲓⲛⲉⲩ = 'this hour, this moment.' The bitter tree of matter still produces bitter fruit in the present age.
'The three strongholds.' ϣⲁⲙⲧ = ϣⲟⲙⲛⲧ 'three'; ⲙⲁⲛⲝⲟⲣⲉ = ⲙⲁⲛϫⲱⲣⲉ 'fortress' (per glossary). The three strongholds where the archons take cover.

Verb ⲣ̄-ⲁⲡⲱⲃⲥ̄ 'to be forgetful/dazed' (Lyc. ⲱⲃⲥ̄ for ⲱⲃϣ̄ 'forget'); split across line break. The archons grew forgetful/confused, then set themselves against the Living Spirit. Tentative reading as 'recoiled/grew dazed.'
ⲥⲉⲍⲙ likely = ⲥⲱϩⲙ̄ 'rebuke, threaten' or related verb of hostile stance; with ⲟⲩⲃⲉ 'against' = 'set themselves against.' Translation tentative.

ⲃⲓⲕ unclear — possibly 'guises, manners, modes of going.' In the context of the Living Spirit appearing in many faces, multitudes, and forms, 'guises' fits the multiple-manifestation register. Tentative.
ⲛⲁⲃ̄ = ⲛⲁϭ 'great'; ⲙⲛⲧⲟⲩⲁ-ⲍⲏⲧ 'state of single-heartedness, unity of mind' (cf. ⲙⲛⲧⲟⲩⲁ 'oneness'). The Living Spirit appears in 'great single-mindednesses' — unified manifestations.
ϣⲛⲟⲩⲍⲙⲉ = ϣ-ⲛⲟⲩⲍⲙ̄ 'to be able to escape.' ⲛ̄ϩⲥⲁⲍⲙⲉ obscure — tentatively 'from his hand/grasp' (possibly Lyc. for ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ̄ or related). The archons cannot escape the Living Spirit's grip.

Translated 'Third Ambassador' per accumulated vocabulary — standard Manichaean cosmological figure (tertius legatus). Note the spelling ⲡⲣⲉⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ (without ⲥ) is a Lycopolitan/scribal variant for ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ; the surrounding lines (e.g. line 22) confirm the standard form is intended.
Read as ϫⲁⲥⲓ-ϩⲏⲧ 'high-hearted' = arrogance, hubris. The Lycopolitan ⲝ for ϫ is regular. Paired here with ⲥⲡⲁⲧⲁⲗⲓⲁ (σπαταλία 'luxury, wantonness'), confirming the moral-vice register.

Translated 'shattered/broken' on the basis of Lycopolitan ⲃⲱϭⲉ (= Sah ⲡⲱϭ/ⲡⲱϭⲉ 'split, break asunder'). The archons of upper and lower sides were broken/shattered — fits the cosmological aftermath of Jesus the Glorious's war. Alternative 'fled' (= ⲡⲱⲧ) is possible but less likely given the qualitative-perfect ⲉⲧⲁⲩⲃⲱϭ̄.

'The Fourth War' — kephalaion structures cosmic battles by ordinal number (ⲡⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧ 'third' figure in line 3, ⲡⲙⲁϩϩⲧⲁⲩ 'fourth' here). The fourth war is led by Jesus the Glorious One, marking the post-cosmogonic stage of redemption.

ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲉ = ⲏⲡⲣⲉ 'fruit'; ⲃⲱϣ Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲱⲱϣ 'be dry, withered.' 'Their fruits dried up' — describes the consequence for the archons after the revelation of the Third Ambassador's image: their seed/fruit withers as the captive light is released.
Lyc ⲁϩⲉⲓ = ⲁϥⲉⲓ 'he came'; ⲁϩⲛ̄ = ⲉϫⲛ̄ 'upon' (Lycopolitan reflex). Translated 'he came down upon' to preserve the directional descent semantics typical of Manichaean salvific action.
Lyc ϩⲱⲕ = Sah ϩⲱⲕ 'strip, despoil, plunder.' 'He stripped' — fits the redemptive-violence schema where Jesus strips the archontic host of its captive light (cf. Col 2:15).
ⲕⲱⲧ here as 'building, structure' (the cosmic edifice), not the homophonous 'builder' or 'pluck.' ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ ⲡⲕⲱⲧ = 'establish the structure' — re-establishment of the cosmic order after the war.

'The purpose of heart of the Greatness' per accumulated vocabulary: ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ = will/intent received from the Father. Here it is the Greatness's commission carried out by Jesus the Glorious in the fourth war.

'The Call and the Answer' — fixed Manichaean technical pair from the cosmogonic Call/Answer of the Living Spirit and First Man. The phrase here is part of an apposition-chain ('which is X, which is Y'), where Counsel (line 29) is identified with the Call and Answer (line 30) — a standard Manichaean theological linkage.

Translated as 'to reign over' — taking ϩⲟⲣⲟ as Lycopolitan verbal infinitive equivalent to ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'to be king' (cf. Lyc ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ in accumulated vocab). The directional ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'over (him/it)' confirms verbal sense. Line 4's ⲧⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'the kingdom' and line 12's ⲡⲟ̄ⲣⲟ 'the king' belong to the same root family.
Left transliterated. May be the tail of a longer noun (e.g. *ⲡⲣⲁⲛⲉⲙⲉⲥ?) or a Greek loan, but no confident identification possible from context alone.
Translated 'the King who shall raise.' ⲟⲣⲟ taken as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣⲣⲟ 'king'; ⲛⲁⲧⲟⲩⲱ as future + ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' (preserving vertical-soteriological semantics per terminology rules).
